data.title: Why OpenAI's Sam Altman says an IPO isn't in the cards this year
data.description:
By Emily Bary

Concerns about AI safety have ramped up, and OpenAI's CEO says now would be an 'ill-advised' time for the ChatGPT creator to go public

Sam Altman of OpenAI says his company will focus on "meeting this moment of what is going to be required for safety and alignment."

As backlash swells against artificial-intelligence companies, the CEO of OpenAI says he won't be testing the public markets this year.

"Given everything happening with safety, right now would be an ill-advised moment to go public, and we don't feel pressure on that," Sam Altman told Fortune in an interview on Friday that was published on Saturday.

He later expressed explicitly that he would not be targeting a 2026 initial public offering. OpenAI didn't immediately respond to a MarketWatch request for further comment.

Rival Anthropic, which operates the Claude model, has already filed confidential IPO paperwork but has yet to put out a public filing. Anthropic didn't immediately respond to a MarketWatch request for comment on its IPO plans.

Opinion: Would you buy stock in a company whose own scientists think the product might kill you?

Altman noted in the Fortune interview that OpenAI would spend time "meeting this moment of what is going to be required for safety and alignment, and how the industry and governments can work together."

AI has been a polarizing technology, and the debate over its implications has only intensified in recent months as OpenAI and its rivals have released even more powerful models. Critics have warned about the potential impact on the job market and the environmental consequences of data centers. Companies have faced increasing local pushback to data-center construction.

See also: Building U.S. data centers is getting so expensive that AI companies are turning overseas

The latest source of public anxiety involves the safety implications of AI as the technology becomes more powerful. Earlier this week, former OpenAI and Anthropic employee Jacob Coxon said he was leaving the latter company - and the industry altogether - because he felt that big AI players were aware of AI's dangerous potential but willing to overlook it in a race to build the best model.

Earlier this year, AI agents were able to escape OpenAI safeguards and breach the systems of Hugging Face, a repository for open-source AI tools. The episode sparked alarm within the AI community.

"It's easy to dismiss this incident because no one was hurt and the economic damage was minimal, but in my opinion, a swarm that possessed greater capabilities but a similar level of misalignment could have caused catastrophic damage," Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said in a blog post on Saturday.

In his post, Amodei called upon the AI industry to slow the pace of model development in order to prevent against safety issues. He also said that Anthropic would bring in third-party evaluators "to verify adherence to safety practices and commitments, report incidents, and help assess the alignment of not just completed AI models but training pipelines and processes."

Altman commented on X that he agreed with Amodei and that OpenAI would "do the same" as far as working with independent evaluators. Elon Musk, whose company SpaceX develops the Grok AI model, weighed in on X as well, writing that Amodei was "right."

It remains to be seen how industry safeguards would play out and if they would be enough to sway public opinion.

"People are starting to wake up, and it's time we wake up all the way," said David Krueger, the founder of Evitable, an organization that warns about AI risks and believes the industry should stop its pursuit of "superintelligence."

Krueger added in emailed comments: "If frontier AI technology is as dangerous as Dario says, then why are we allowing these companies to pick their own regulators and set their own pace?"

-Emily Bary

data.title: Agog-Supported Works Win Two of Three Immersive Prizes at the 83rd Venice International Film Festival
data.description:
Agog-Supported Works Win Two of Three Immersive Prizes at the 83rd Venice International Film Festival

Agog-Supported Works Win Two of Three Immersive Prizes at the 83rd Venice International Film Festival

PR Newswire

LOS ANGELES, Sept. 12, 2026

Out of the Ashes receives the Venice Immersive Special Jury Prize and Empire at Sea receives the Venice Immersive Achievement Prize; the two projects offer distinct approaches to climate storytelling

LOS ANGELES, Sept. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Two projects supported by Agog: The Immersive Media Institute won two of the three prizes awarded today in the Venice Immersive competition at the 83rd Venice International Film Festival. Out of the Ashes, co-directed by Rory Mitchell and Nonny de la Peña, received the Venice Immersive Special Jury Prize. Empire at Sea, created and directed by Peter Flaherty, earned the Venice Immersive Achievement Prize.

The awards celebrate two distinct approaches to climate storytelling. Out of the Ashes is a virtual-reality documentary about loss, memory, resilience, and rebuilding after the January 2025 Los Angeles fires. Empire at Sea is an interactive solarpunk augmented-reality drama that asks audiences to confront questions of sustainability, migration, inclusion, and collective survival.

Agog-Supported Works Win Two of Three Immersive Prizes at the 83rd Venice International Film Festival

"Wendy Schmidt and I founded Agog on the belief that immersive media can bring people closer to urgent issues and help them imagine what change could look like," said Chip Giller, co-founder and executive director of Agog. "At Venice, we saw creators expand what these emerging technologies can do—and audiences responded in deeply personal ways. Out of the Ashes brought people from around the world close to the human toll of the Los Angeles fires, and many saw echoes of what their own communities have experienced. Empire at Sea shows new possibilities for filmmaking by pairing cinematic performance and an accomplished cast with the power of immersive media. Seeing both works recognized on a global stage makes us more excited than ever about immersive media's potential to advance storytelling, contribute to social change, and serve the public good."

"Out of the Ashes and Empire at Sea are ambitious, deeply human works that demonstrate the creative range of immersive storytelling," said Liz Rosenthal and Michel Reilhac, curators of Venice Immersive. "Agog made a meaningful contribution to Venice Immersive this year, not only through its support of three projects selected for competition, but also by creating spaces where artists, producers, technologists, and changemakers could experiment, exchange ideas, and form new connections. That combination of supporting individual projects and investing in the wider ecosystem is exactly what an emerging field needs to grow."

About Out of the Ashes
Narrated by award-winning actor Courtney B. Vance, Out of the Ashes places audiences within the events and aftermath of the Los Angeles wildfires. The 26-minute documentary combines first-person storytelling with volumetric reconstructions of participants' homes, created in part from their own family photos and videos. It closes by highlighting community organizations leading recovery efforts, including My Tribe Rise, Evolve Altadena, and the Palisades Recovery Coalition.

The work was created by Rory Mitchell and Nonny de la Peña and co-produced by The Mercantile Agency, Emblematic Group, and Arizona State University's MA in Narrative and Emerging Media program, with support from Agog and the MacArthur Foundation.

Out of the Ashes assets: project page | press kit

About Empire at Sea
Empire at Sea is a 22-minute interactive augmented-reality drama about climate scientists building a sustainable community on a remote oil rig after a catastrophe cuts them off from the mainland. Up to 10 audience members experience cinematic holograms around a custom interactive LED table and navigate together a story about science, sustainability, immigration, and community.

The work was created, directed, and produced by Peter Flaherty; commissioned by Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts and ASU Gammage; developed with Flaherty Pictures, 4DV.ai, and NightLight Labs; and supported by Agog, the Schwarzman Center at Yale University, and the Alfred P. Sloan Foundation. It is scheduled to be presented at Lincoln Center in January 2027.

Empire at Sea assets: project page | website | press kit

Agog at Venice Immersive
Agog supported three projects selected for this year's Venice Immersive competition. The third, Solwata, is a mixed-reality documentary that brings audiences into the lives of communities in Solomon Islands confronting rising seas, displacement, and planned relocation. Created by NowHere Media and co-produced by Human Rights Watch and Agog, the experience is narrated and executive produced by Mark Ruffalo. Following its Venice premiere, Solwata is now being presented at the Toronto International Film Festival's Innovation Hub through Sept. 16. It will next appear at the BFI London Film Festival and COP31, the annual United Nations climate change conference.

Beyond its involvement with the three projects, Agog partnered with Venice Immersive on the occasion of the festival's 10th anniversary to shape discussions about what the next decade could hold, with a focus on impact. Throughout the festival, Agog convened creators, nonprofit leaders, funders, technologists, and cultural leaders for programming including a Smart Glasses Petting Zoo offering hands-on access to the latest emerging technology to consider ways it could be harnessed for storytelling and social good, an imagination workshop focused on expanding what is possible in immersive storytelling, and hands-on- conversations about new creative possibilities and the opportunities for immersive media to spur social change.

These activities are part of Agog's broader efforts to champion ambitious work, connect people across the immersive ecosystem, and help immersive media develop with public purpose at its center. Learn more

About Agog: The Immersive Media Institute
Agog: The Immersive Media Institute is a philanthropic organization founded by Chip Giller and Wendy Schmidt that is dedicated to helping creators and nonprofit leaders use immersive media—including virtual, augmented, and mixed reality—to imagine and build a more connected, just, and compassionate world. Agog operates as a field builder and creative partner, supporting immersive storytellers whose work addresses urgent social and environmental challenges. Learn more at agog.org

data.title: Aster Guardians Global Nursing Award 2026 Names Agimol Pradeep From United Kingdom Winner of USD 250,000 Prize
data.description:
Aster Guardians Global Nursing Award 2026 Names Agimol Pradeep From United Kingdom Winner of USD 250,000 Prize

From more than 134,000 registrations spanning 214 countries and economies, Nurse Agimol Pradeep from United Kingdom has been announced as the winner of the Aster Guardians Global Nursing Award 2026. A Senior Transplant Coordinator at King’s College Hospital and Honorary Senior Lecturer at the University of Salford, UK, she was recognised with USD 250,000 at a prestigious ceremony held in Kochi, India.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260912257725/en/

Nurse Agimol Pradeep - Aster Guardians Global Nursing Award 2026 Winner (Photo: AETOSWire)

Since its launch in 2021, the Aster Guardians Global Nursing Award has grown into a global platform that celebrates nurses who are advancing the profession and creating meaningful change. The award was presented by Shri V. D. Satheesan, Hon’ble Chief Minister of Keralam, in presence of Dr. Azad Moopen and Alisha Moopen. The ceremony also featured a special message from Dr. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, Director-General of the WHO, applauding Aster’s role in celebrating the contributions of nurses worldwide.

Nurse Agimol Pradeep said, “I am deeply honoured to receive the Aster Guardians Global Nursing Award. I hope to use this opportunity to expand organ and stem cell donation, while empowering nurses and strengthening the global nursing workforce to drive lasting change.”

Dr. Azad Moopen, Founder Chairman, Aster DM Healthcare stated,“Nurse Agimol Pradeep’s achievement embodies the expertise, courage, compassion and unwavering commitment that define exceptional nursing. These are the qualities at the heart of the Aster Guardians Global Nursing Award, which was established to recognise and elevate the vital contributions of nurses worldwide.”

Alisha Moopen, Managing Director and Group CEO, Aster DM Healthcare added, “Nurse Agimol has shown us that meaningful change can begin anywhere through a single nurse determined to solve a problem. Stories of our top 10 finalists demonstrate that nurses are not only essential to delivering healthcare; they are shaping how healthcare evolves.”

About Aster DM Healthcare:

Founded in 1987 by Dr. Azad Moopen, Aster DM Healthcare is a leading integrated healthcare provider, with a strong presence across seven countries. Aster is committed to the vision of providing accessible and high-quality healthcare, from primary to quaternary services, with its promise of “We will treat you well.”

data.title: Calvin Klein Collection by Veronica Leoni Spring 2027 Runway Show Presented in New York City
data.description:
Calvin Klein Collection by Veronica Leoni Spring 2027 Runway Show Presented in New York City

Calvin Klein, Inc., part of PVH Corp. [NYSE:PVH], presented yesterday the Calvin Klein Collection Spring 2027 runway show by Creative Director Veronica Leoni at Terminal Warehouse in New York City. The Collection was a continuation of the exploration of American Minimalism.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260912623744/en/

Calvin Klein Collection

“American Minimalism was a discipline of removal: take away everything that does not carry the work, until only what is necessary remains,” said Veronica Leoni, Creative Director of Calvin Klein Collection. “Calvin drew from that and turned it toward the body. I turn it toward the woman inside it. My minimalism begins there, in the relation between design and a body, with nothing in between. Take everything away. What is left is desire.”

The Collection is built from the house’s foundational pieces—the coat, the shirt, tailoring, the trouser, the pencil skirt, the slip—with proportions that run longer and narrower, or are cinched at the waist. Tailoring is cut thin and crisp in cotton and lightweight wool: a three-button cotton suit, slim, with the ease of a t-shirt, and a broader-shouldered jacket made to be layered. Slip and t-shirt dresses are cut as full bias evening dresses. Extra-fine silk knit tees and color-blocked baseball shirts in silk cady carry the Collection’s American sportswear vernacular with denim, leather, laser-cut suede and delicate flashes of underwear rounding out the Collection. The palette moves through a multitude of whites and blacks, with scarlet, bright yellow, royal blue, cherry and light citron, and a check drawn from and inspired by Georgia O’Keeffe’s wardrobe.

Accessories are shaped by purpose and practicality. Metal headbands pull the hair back. Scarves drape and come to a point. Bags are enlarged in proportion, sleek and structural or soft and slouchy, with a new triangular, origami-like shape.

The show took place at Terminal Warehouse, the block-long brick warehouse built in 1891 to the design of George B. Mallory and a landmark of New York’s industrial architecture. Inside, three floor sculptures by Walter De Maria are installed along the runway, allowing audience and models to move through it. The soundtrack by Kid Harpoon features Laurie Anderson and Solange over a score of sustained, repeating figures.

In attendance at the show were ROSALÍA, Teyana Taylor, Tate McRae, Sadie Sink, Ling Ling Kwong, Solange, Emily Ratajkowski, Pamela Anderson, Gemma Chan, Katie Holmes, Jason Bard Yarmosky, Benito Skinner, Mary Beth Barone, Maya Boyd, Supriya Ganesh, St. Vincent, Alex Eala, Giulia Be, Misty Copeland, Iris Law, Lila Moss, Sabrina Elba, Jose Alvarado, 3House, Marcus and Iris Ericsson, Antwaun Sargent, Kid Harpoon, Bethann Hardison, Kitty Ca$h and more dressed in Calvin Klein Collection. Other guests included Elizabeth Saltzman, Derek Blasberg, Lauren Santo Domingo, Eva Chen, Brandice Daniel, Tommy Ton, Steven Kolb, Phil Oh, Dirk Scanden and more.

Other guests include Nara Smith, Wisdom Kaye, Madeline Argy, Jake Shane, Yesly Dimate, Ashtin Earle, Isabelle Allain, Natalia Bryant, Chriselle Lim, Charli D’Amelio, Nai Devora, Lily Chee, Jordan Daniels, Marlon Garcia, Ruby Lyn, Alioune Badara-Fall, Sandra Shehab, Jordan Rand, Isan Elba, Enya Umanzor, Jacob Rott, Bach Buquen, Rebecca Donaldson, Paola Locatelli, Ting Ting Lai, Tamu McPherson, Sam Salter, Maritz Hau, Tony Ozkan, Laura Abla, Alexa Chung, Camila Coelho, Maria Bottle, Jorge Patino, Arantza Goett, Jordana Maia, Thomas Chung Manirat, Seira Anzai, Kemio, Sea Tawinan, Bambi Northwood-Bluth and more, who were dressed in styles from the world of Calvin Klein, including Calvin Klein Collection, Calvin Klein Jeans, tailored suiting and apparel.

data.title: A Green Beret's Humanitarian Mission to Remove Ukraine's Landmines Now Streaming on Prime Video in the U.S. and UK
data.description:
A Green Beret's Humanitarian Mission to Remove Ukraine's Landmines Now Streaming on Prime Video in the U.S. and UK

A Green Beret's Humanitarian Mission to Remove Ukraine's Landmines Now Streaming on Prime Video in the U.S. and UK

PR Newswire

PENSACOLA, Fla., Sept. 12, 2026

PENSACOLA, Fla., Sept. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Safe Ground: A Green Beret's Mission to Remove Ukraine's Landmines, a powerful new documentary highlighting the story of Ryan Hendrickson, a retired U.S. Army Green Beret, Purple Heart and Silver Star recipient, author, and founder of Tip of the Spear Landmine Removal, is now available for streaming on Prime Video in the U.S. and UK. The title is available to stream with a Prime membership as well as to rent or buy.

The premiere date, September 12, holds deeply personal significance: September 12th is Ryan Hendrickson's "Alive Day" — the anniversary of the day he survived stepping on an improvised explosive device (IED) in Afghanistan, a date that marks both the moment he nearly lost his life and the beginning of the mission that would come to define it.

Safe Ground follows Ryan Hendrickson, a retired U.S. Army Green Beret, Purple Heart recipient, author, and humanitarian whose experience with explosive devices nearly cost him his life.

"When I stepped on that IED in Afghanistan, I thought my story was over." Hendrickson said, "Instead, it gave me the clarity to understand what I was really meant to do. Every landmine we pull out of the ground in Ukraine is a life that gets to continue — a farmer who can work his field, a child who can walk to school. This film captures why we do this work, and I hope it shows people that the men and women who serve this country never stop serving."

In 2010, while conducting combat operations in Afghanistan, Ryan stepped on an IED while attempting to rescue an Afghan soldier. After a remarkable recovery and return to active duty, he eventually carried his experience into a new mission.

Through Tip of the Spear Landmine Removal, Ryan and his team work to remove these deadly remnants of war, restore land to safe use, and protect the farmers, families, and children who live with the fear that any step could be their last.

"Ryan's story is a testament to what happens when a warrior's training meets an unwavering sense of purpose. At Amazon, we believe the skills forged in military service don't expire at the end of a deployment — they find new missions." Charlotte La Belle, Global Head of Military Affairs at Amazon said; "Our relationship with Tip of the Spear is about demonstrating that the same veterans who defended our nation are now leading some of the most critical humanitarian work on the planet."

"Ryan's mission has not only saved Ukrainian lives, but it has also given American veterans a new sense of purpose," said Colby Barrett, producer of Safe Ground and the Faith in War series and former U.S. Marine Corps Captain. "I'm grateful to Prime Video for helping us share Ryan's story of service, sacrifice, and hope. The Ukrainian people want what we want — family, freedom, and a safe place to call home — and Ryan and the Tip of the Spear are making that possible, one mine removal at a time." 

SAFE GROUND is the story of a soldier who returned to the weapon that nearly killed him — not to fight another war, but to create a path toward safety, recovery, and hope.

WATCH THE FILM & EXPLORE THE SERIES

Streaming on Prime Video — September 12, 2026

  • Trailer
  • Watch on Prime Video

SAFE GROUND is part of FAITH IN WAR, a five-film documentary series from the award-winning creators of A Faith Under Siege. The Simply Good Foods Company (SMPL) Class Action Lawsuit Seeks Recovery for Investors; October 13, 2026, Deadline - Contact Kessler Topaz Meltzer & Check, LLP

The Simply Good Foods Company (SMPL) Class Action Lawsuit Seeks Recovery for Investors; October 13, 2026, Deadline - Contact Kessler Topaz Meltzer & Check, LLP

PR Newswire

RADNOR, Pa., Sept. 12, 2026

Did you buy SMPL common stock between October 24, 2024 and April 8, 2026?

Affected SMPL Investor Summary

  • Who: The Simply Good Foods Company (NASDAQ: SMPL)
  • What: Securities fraud class action lawsuit filed
  • Class Period: October 24, 2024 through April 8, 2026
  • Deadline to Seek Lead Plaintiff Status: October 13, 2026
  • Key Lawsuit Allegations: Material misstatements and/or omissions concerning the company's strategy going into its acquisition of OWYN
  • Investor Action: Contact Kessler Topaz Meltzer & Check, LLP (www.ktmc.com) for recovery options

RADNOR, Pa., Sept. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Kessler Topaz Meltzer & Check, LLP (www.ktmc.com), a nationally recognized securities litigation law firm, informs investors that a securities fraud class action lawsuit has been filed against The Simply Good Foods Company ("Good Foods") (NASDAQ: SMPL) on behalf of those who purchased or acquired Good Foods common stock between October 24, 2024 and April 8, 2026, inclusive. The lawsuit is filed in the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York and is captioned Monroe County Employees' Retirement System v. The Simply Good Foods Company, No. 26-cv-06971 (S.D.N.Y.). Investors have until October 13, 2026, to file for lead plaintiff status. 

CONTACT KTMC TO DISCUSS YOUR LEGAL RIGHTS: 
If you purchased or acquired Good Foods common stock and have lost money on your investment, please provide your information here:

https://www.ktmc.com/smpl-the-simply-good-foods-company-class-action-lawsuit?utm_source=PR_Newswire&utm_medium=pressrelease&utm_campaign=smpl&mktm=PR

You can also contact attorney Jonathan Naji, Esq. by calling (484) 270-1453 or by email at info@ktmc.com. There is no cost or obligation to speak with an attorney.

To view the Good Foods video on YouTube, click here: https://youtu.be/zH6SYi5Gj_4 

THE SIMPLY GOOD FOODS COMPANY CLASS ACTION LAWSUIT - COMPLAINT ALLEGATION SUMMARY:
Good Foods develops and sells packaged health foods and snacks under its portfolio brands that includes Quest, Atkins, and OWYN. On April 29, 2024, Good Foods announced an agreement to acquire OWYN for $280 million in an all-cash transaction, in a transaction that Good Foods claimed would diversify the company's portfolio and strengthen its presence with retail customers. The acquisition was completed on June 13, 2024, and by that October, Good Foods stated that the integration of OWYN was "progressing as planned" and assured investors that it "remain[ed] confident" in Good Food's ability to "effectively integrate OWYN."

The complaint alleges that, throughout the Class Period, Defendants made materially false and/or misleading statements, as well as failed to disclose material facts about the company's business, operations, and prospects. Specifically, Defendants misrepresented and/or failed to disclose that: (1) following the acquisition, key managers fled Good Foods; (2) Good Foods implemented a layered organizational structure in an attempt to remedy the personnel loss, which instead was later described as bloated and lacking strategic cohesion; (3) the company experienced product quality control issues due in part to switching to an inferior supplier, causing negatively impacted sales and customer loyalty; (4) execution failures and increased management costs led to margin erosion, leading Good Foods to begin heavy discounting activities and cutting brand support; and (5) as a result of the foregoing, Defendants' statements about the company's business, operations, and prospects were materially false and misleading and/or lacked a reasonable basis at all relevant times.

Why did Good Foods' Stock Drop?
On April 9, 2026, Good Foods announced its second quarter 2026 earnings results, revealing that customer consumption had plummeted across all of its brands. Notably, Good Foods revealed that OWYN's quarterly sales had contracted by nearly 17% year-over-year, a start contract from the double-digit growth that Good Foods previously highlighted. In the corresponding call, Good Foods admitted, among other things, that the company had "made some strategic choices" that" ultimately weakened" its performance. On this news, the price of Good Foods common stock declined more than 27% over a two-day trading period.

WHAT THE SIMPLY GOOD FOODS COMPANY INVESTORS CAN DO NOW:

  1. File to be lead plaintiff by October 13, 2026.
  2. Contact KTMC for a free case evaluation. All representation is on a contingency fee basis, there is no cost to you.
  3. Retain counsel of choice or take no action.

THE LEAD PLAINTIFF PROCESS FOR THE SIMPLY GOOD FOODS COMPANY. INVESTORS:
Good Foods investors may, no later than October 13, 2026, seek to be appointed as a lead plaintiff representative of the class through Kessler Topaz Meltzer & Check, LLP or other counsel, or may choose to do nothing and remain an absent class member. A lead plaintiff is a representative party who acts on behalf of all class members in directing the litigation. The lead plaintiff is usually the investor or small group of investors who have the largest financial interest and who are also adequate and typical of the proposed class of investors. The lead plaintiff selects counsel to represent the lead plaintiff and the class and these attorneys, if approved by the court, are lead or class counsel. Your ability to share in any recovery is not affected by the decision of whether or not to serve as a lead plaintiff.

Kessler Topaz Meltzer & Check, LLP encourages Good Foods investors to contact the firm for more information.

ABOUT KESSLER TOPAZ MELTZER & CHECK, LLP (KTMC): 
Kessler Topaz Meltzer & Check, LLP (KTMC) is a leading U.S. plaintiff-side law firm focused on securities-fraud class actions and global investor protection. The firm represents individual investors as well as institutions, such as major pension funds, asset managers, and international investors. KTMC has led some of the largest recoveries in securities litigation and has been recognized by peers and the legal media with numerous accolades, including being recognized in Chambers & Partners USA 2026 as a Band 1 Top Firm in Securities and Class Actions, Legal 500's Tier 1 Rankings for Securities and M&A Litigation, The National Law Journal's Plaintiff's Hot List and Trailblazers in Plaintiffs' Law, BTI Consulting Group's Honor Roll of Most Feared Law Firms, The Legal Intelligencer's Class Action Firm of the Year, Lawdragon's Leading Plaintiff Financial Lawyers, and Law360's Titans of the Plaintiffs Bar. The firm operates globally with offices in Pennsylvania and California. KTMC has recovered over $25 billion for our clients and the classes they represent. The complaint in this matter was not filed by KTMC.
